subject: BUG-267: the CLIENT keeps its own stale house list, and past 5 mismatches it LOCKS THE STUDENT OUT
description:
Found by the adversarial reviewer 2026-09-07 while clearing the BUG-264/266 functions patch. _app/components/XPCalculator.js:25 and _app/components/FirestoreManager.js:1405 each hard-code their OWN _KNOWN_HOUSES and their own doubled-prefix rejection, entirely independent of functions/index.js. Both are missing eth, ala, career and windows -- the four houses just added server-side after enumerating every real completion id in production. XPCalculator.js:55-96 (_checkIntegrity) counts anything failing its LOCAL _isValidId as 'garbage', and past FIVE such entries writes hexworth_integrity:'violated' to localStorage, which IntegrityLockscreen.js consumes to lock the student out. So a student who legitimately completes several eth or ala modules accumulates 'garbage' by the client's stale reckoning and can be locked out of the platform for doing real coursework. NOT IMMINENT, AND NOT CREATED BY TONIGHT'S DEPLOY: the client list was already stale before it, and current volumes are low -- eth 9 completions, ala 2, career 1, windows 1, spread across 3874 users -- so nobody is near the threshold of 5 today. But the server now RECOGNISES those ids as legitimate, so the content can grow without the server objecting while the client keeps counting it as corruption. FIX: sync both client copies to the server list (add eth, ala, career, windows) and remove the same key.startsWith(house + '-') clause that wrongly rejected forge-forge-core2-virtualization-lab. Verify against _tools/progress-snapshot/snapshots/ that 0 of 7528 real ids are counted as garbage by the client rule. BETTER, IF IT CAN BE MADE TO WORK: three hard-coded copies of one list is the actual defect -- this is the fourth time in one session that fixing one copy of a rule left another copy wrong. A punitive lockout keyed off a list that drifts is a design that will keep costing students access.
[2026-09-07 05:05] CORRECTION TO MY OWN SEVERITY CALL, found by Chris at the quality gate. I reported this as 'NOT IMMINENT -- current volumes are low, nobody is near the threshold of 5 today'. That was WRONG, and wrong in a specific way worth remembering: I counted only the ids the NEW 22-house list rejects, and never replayed the OLD 11-house list that was actually running in XPCalculator. I measured the fix instead of the bug. Chris replayed the pre-fix list against the same snapshot: the account holding lab_ala_l02/lab_ala_l03 had FOURTEEN garbage hits under the old list -- nearly 3x past the lockout threshold of 5, i.e. already eligible for IntegrityLockscreen to lock them out. After the fix that same account sits at 2. So this was not a future landmine, it was live, and the fix is a 14 -> 2 reduction for a real account rather than the cosmetic tidy-up my summary implied. THE LESSON, which generalises: when judging whether a bug is urgent, replay the BROKEN rule against the data. Measuring what the FIXED rule rejects tells you the fix is clean; it tells you nothing about who the bug was already hurting. RESOLVED at df8f7b367: all three lists unified to the same 22 houses, GUARD-07 added as a cross-file comparison so the drift cannot recur silently, Chris PASS recorded after he independently re-derived every load-bearing number.
